supplementation of both forms (selenite and yeast) of selenium into the basal diet of laying hents significantly influences the concentration Se in blood of hens and most physical qualitative parameters of their eggs.
supplementation of both forms selenium into the diet significantly influences the concentra tion in blood of laying hen, and most of the qualitative parameters of eggs.

supplementation of both forms (SS and SY) of selenium into the laying hens basal diet significantly influences concentration of Se in laying hens blood and most of the qualitative parameters of eggs (except eggshell quality and eggshell weight).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary supplementation of sodium selenite or selenized brewer’s yeast on the qualitative parameters of eggs in laying hens.
the influence of dietary supplementation with sodium selenate or selenized brewer’s yeast on selected quality parameters of laying hens’ eggs.
a study of the effects of supplementation into laying h hens’ basal diets of sodium selenite and selenized yeast on the concentration of Se and some qualitative parameters of eggs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SY supplementation of the basal diet of laying h ens at the dose of 0.9mg Se/kg DM has positive effect on the qualitative parameters of eggs and is recommended for the commercial practice.
supplementation of SY at the dose of 0.9mg/kg DM is the most efficient way to enhance Se concentration in laying hens blood and to improve the quality of eggs.

the SY supplementation of basal diet is more effective in increasing Se concentration in blood of laying hen and in increasing some qualitative parameters of eggs than the SS supplementation of basal diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supplementation with sodium selenate and selenized yeast had positive effects on some egg quality parameters.
the supplementation of both forms and both doses of Se in diet of laying h ens has a positive effect on the qualitative parameters of eggs.
supplementation of laying hens’ diet with selenium in the form of SY at a dose of 0.9mg Se/kg of DM significantly improves the quality of eggs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supplementation of both forms and doses of selenium into the basal diet of laying hents had a significant effect in the concentration of selenium in the blood of laying hents.
the supplementation of SY at dose 0.4 and 0.9mg Se/kg DM significantly influences the concentration Se in blood of layers and most of the qualitative parameters of eggs.

the supplementation of both forms selenium into the diet has a significant impact on the concentration of Se, egg weight, egg albumen weight, egg album width, egg albumen height, Haugh units and egg yolk ratio in the egg.
